title: Charlie Christian, Freddie Green and Lester Young's wire cutters
summary: Rowe is surprised to hear Christian chomping like Freddie Green; Buckingham tells Sweets Edison's story of Lester Young cutting the wires on Green's amplifier.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: There’s some real gems on the thing and I was listening to the one, “Stompin’ at the Savoy” with the Benny Goodman Sextet. And I hadn’t looked at the personnel but I am hearing this chomp-chomp-chomp-chomp — and I go man, Freddie Green’s really going at it. And then I looked and it was Charlie Christian. And that surprised me I guess because I’m not sure I had heard Charlie Christian do that. I was more familiar with his soloing.

On the electric. But they could do — now I’ll tell you a funny story that Sweets told me, Sweets Edison. Of course Freddie Green was the guy on the archtop acoustic rhythm. Although Chet Atkins knew everybody. He told me the best rhythm guitarist he ever heard was um — Homer and Jethro — Homer Hanes. Remember Homer and Jethro? The guitar and mandolin kind of comedy duo? He said Homer Hanes was the best of the old archtop rhythm players. Freddie Green was second. And those guys, the action on their guitars was up this high. I mean it was impossible to fret those things, but Freddie Green was the guy, man. But Sweets told me that one time Freddie Green shows up with an amplifier and a pick-up on his guitar. And you know, he said they hated this thing, because the way he went chomp-chomp-chomp you know every beat is a chord change. And so during a break Lester Young took a pair of wire cutters and went in the amp and started snipping wires. So he came back and said Freddie Green gave up on the electric guitar. That’s why you never heard Freddie Green playing an electric. But you know I haven’t looked at the box set in years. I’ve got copies at home but I think I’ve pointed this out, some of it was re-done in the studio and I’ve even got the pictures I think I put in there. I know I’ve got one at the house. And it’s Freddie Green and Charlie Christian and Basie and Goodman, Jo Jones and you know, Lester Young, Buck Clayton. So they re-

did some things in the studio. And I talk about it in there. They’d never talked about it before but Mr. Hammond had told me. And in all my delving around and all the notes and tapes and everything I found all that stuff too. But yeah, not too bad to have Freddie Green and Charlie Christian playing, and Lester Young trading off with them. I know it’s, like I say, heavy stuff.
